taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from Introduction to hematology.

words.clue: The continuous process by which all blood cells are produced from a common ancestor in the bone marrow.
Hormone produced by kidney cells that stimulates the production of red blood cells.
Growth factor produced by the liver and kidney that drives the production of platelets.
The production of red blood cells through sequential maturation stages in the bone marrow.
An immature red blood cell containing RNA that serves as a quality-control metric for bone marrow function.
The erythroblast stage where cytoplasm appears blue-pink as hemoglobin accumulates during development.
The erythroblast stage characterized by dark blue cytoplasm due to high RNA content.
The earliest and largest stage of red blood cell development with a large pale nucleus and prominent nucleoli.
The oxygen-carrying protein that accumulates in developing red blood cells during the polychromatic stage.
The primary blood-forming organ from birth onward where haematopoiesis occurs continuously.
